description:
Surfaced 2026-05-12 by PRINCIPAL after a STRABO claim about jallum/beadwork upstream code (internal/issue/id.go:128 containing `matches = append(matches, matches)`) reached substrate-tier as a "drive-by upstream PR" candidate. Verification at the propagation boundary showed the claim was fabricated — no commit in the file's entire 3-commit history (Feb 21-22, 2026) ever contained the claimed code; the line has always been the structurally-correct `append(matches, id)` or `append(matches, name)`.

The chain that almost-but-didn't fail:
1. STRABO read source and produced a research artifact citing a non-existent bug.
2. Project-tier PLINY/POLYBIUS propagated the claim into a substrate-tier relay.
3. Substrate-tier POLYBIUS almost drafted a GitHub issue against jallum's repo.
4. Only the "stop guessing, look at the code" reflex (PRINCIPAL-reinforced earlier in the session) caught it at the drafting boundary.

PRINCIPAL's proposed structural fix: extend VERA verification to STRABO claims. Same pipeline-redundancy property that catches CATO-vs-VERA defect classes, generalized to STRABO claims.

## The discipline

**STRABO claims aren't load-bearing until VERA verifies them.** Treat STRABO output as preliminary; VERA-verified citations become canonical. Substrate-tier propagation requires VERA verification at the boundary.

## VERA verification probe shapes per claim type

| Claim type | Probe |
|---|---|
| Source-code citation (file:line at commit) | Re-fetch source at the claimed commit + grep for the claimed line. Match or fail. ~3s cost. |
| Documentation citation (URL + paragraph) | Re-fetch + read surrounding context. Confirm STRABO interpretation isn't stretched. Low cost. |
| Behavioral claim about a tool/library | Re-run the behavior; check it survives. Moderate cost. |
| Synthesis claim ("every mature project has X") | Sample N of the underlying sources independently; confirm STRABO pattern claim holds across the sample. Higher cost; also higher overreach risk. |

The first two are cheap and would have caught the 2026-05-12 STRABO fabrication. The fourth is expensive but is where STRABO is most likely to overreach (synthesis-shape claims are where confirmation bias compounds).

## Substrate touch-points

Three files in substrate need edits:

1. **CAPTAIN_VERA.md** — broaden verification scope. New section in the role file's "what VERA verifies" enumeration: STRABO research artifacts (cited claims independently verified before substrate-tier propagation).

2. **CAPTAIN_STRABO.md** — note that STRABO output is preliminary until VERA-verified. Same pattern as DAEDALUS designs being preliminary until ARGUS reviews. Self-marking discipline: STRABO surfaces claims with explicit "needs VERA verification" tags when the claim is intended for substrate-tier or upstream-project propagation.

3. **MAJOR_PLINY.md dispatch-protocol** — when STRABO is dispatched in a gauntlet that produces substrate-tier or upstream-bound output, VERA is dispatched on the artifact afterward with a citation-verification brief. PLINY scope-decides whether the VERA round is full (every citation) or sampled (random N of citations).

## Gauntlet

DAEDALUS-light + ADA + CATO. Substrate doc edits across three role files + a brief addition to PLINY's dispatch protocol. ~50-100 LOC of substrate prose.

The DAEDALUS-light step picks:
- Sampling policy for synthesis claims (full vs N=k random vs risk-weighted)
- Whether STRABO self-tags claims as "needs-vera" or every STRABO artifact gets blanket VERA dispatch
- How VERA's verdict feeds back into the artifact (overlay annotations? separate verdict file? amended artifact?)

## Sequencing

P2. Substrate hygiene that prevents a class of failure (fabricated agent claims reaching upstream / substrate canon). Bundle with the other in-flight stoa substrate tickets (vmc, rno, nax, 148, etc.) when next substrate-grooming dispatch fires.

## Out of scope

- Verifying every claim in every CAPTAIN's output (over-extension; CAPTAIN-tier work is already verified by the gauntlet downstream)
- New verification seat (over-engineering; VERA generalizes cleanly)
- Penalty mechanism for STRABO making bad claims (out of scope; substrate-discipline is process, not punishment)

## Empirical anchor

2026-05-12 — STRABO claim about internal/issue/id.go:128 in the project-tier bw scaling research artifact. Three-commit history check at file's lifetime confirms the bug never existed. Verification cost was ~10 seconds of curl + grep. Cost of NOT verifying would have been a wrong-bug GitHub issue against jallum's actively-maintained upstream, with reputational cost to PRINCIPAL as the reporter and process-credibility cost to the substrate.
title: VERA verifies STRABO: extend independent-verification discipline to research artifacts
